finding: Round 8's fix moved the derivation window's authority from the script into `spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md`, and nothing binds that document back to §7.1. The check now verifies the guard document's INTERNAL consistency and never its CONFORMANCE to the spec — so any self-consistent window ships green, including one that is not the window §7.1 mandates. Reproduced in a fresh clone of 66ec712, populating the list exactly as the first task will: (M11) rewrite the document with window `v0.31.2`..`v0.33.0`, its own re-derived summary (173 test functions across 47 files) and its own 173-entry list -> exit 0. (M12) same with `v0.30.0`..`v0.33.0`, 272 functions across 69 files, 272 entries -> exit 0. (M13) same with `v0.33.0~10`..`v0.33.0`, 3 functions across 3 files, 3 entries -> exit 0. In all three §7.1 still reads "added between the `v0.32.0` and `v0.33.0` tags", the check exits 0 with no PENDING and no warning, and the §7 sweep's entire scope is whatever the document declared. M13 is the sharp case: §7.1's named silent-failure rule, "An empty guard list is a failed derivation, never a result", is enforced by the `if not derived` branch at exactly zero and nowhere else, so a derivation that returns 3 of the mandated 100 is indistinguishable from a correct one. This is the same escape class round 8 recorded as fixed (M9: "the check re-derives the old window and agrees with itself") with the direction inverted — it now re-derives the NEW window and agrees with itself — and the relocation made it worse in one respect: authority now sits in the document produced after review closes by the very task the check polices, whereas §7.1, which states the same fact, is the reviewed artifact and is the one home the check never reads. The asymmetry is visible inside the script itself: `check_repo_claim` reads a claim out of `spec/0.34.0.md`, so reading the spec is already established; only the window is exempt. Not hypothetical — the window has been rewritten three times during this review loop (audit-round commits -> touched -> added).

resolved.evidence: The spec is now the authority for the window: the check extracts the tag pair from section 7.1 and fails when the guard document's command disagrees. Mutation-tested with the reported counter-example (a v0.33.0~10 window plus a matching three-entry list), which now fails.

suggestion: Bind the document's window to the spec's. §7.1 already states the tags in a matchable form; extract them (e.g. a pattern over "between the `<tag>` and `<tag>` tags" in SPEC_DOC) and require the tag pair in the guard document's `git diff` line to equal them, failing with both pairs named when they differ. That keeps round 8's property (the rule is read from the document, so the script holds no third copy) while removing the freedom that makes M11-M13 pass: the document may still state the command, but it may not choose a different window from the one review converged on.

finding: Round 9 idx 1 (coverage-boundary-stated-by-kind-not-location, medium) was recorded fixed with 'The coverage line states the boundary by location -- two claims in two named files -- rather than by claim kind, so it no longer reads as a promise over every number in the spec.' Verified against the tree rather than the evidence line: the repair landed in scripts/check-measured-claims.py only. spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md -- the artifact §7.1 designates, and the only place the spec sends a reader for what the check covers -- still closes with 'The check states its own coverage boundary on every run: re-derivable counts only.' That is verbatim the by-kind formulation the finding disproved, and it is now also false about the check's output: the line printed today reads 'coverage: guards two claims only -- the guard-test window and list in spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md, and the repository test-function count in spec/0.34.0.md. Every other number in either document is unchecked and remains reportable.' The same paragraph also under-describes the check after rounds 8 and 9: it says the check fails 'when the numbers above go stale, when the derivation returns nothing, or when the claim is reworded past the pattern that finds it' and names none of the three properties those rounds added -- the pinned documented command and match rule, the set comparison of the list, and the placeholder contradiction. All three are real (mutation-tested in a clone at 66ec712: rule reworded -> exit 1; window moved to v0.31.2..v0.33.0 with the numbers kept -> exit 1; --no-ext-diff dropped from the documented command -> exit 1; 100 fabricated entries with the declaration deleted -> exit 1; entries alongside the declaration -> exit 1; the true 100-entry list, bare or as bullets -> exit 0). So the one fact 'what this check guarantees' now has two homes that disagree, and the surviving stale home is the one §7.1 points at.

resolved.evidence: The guard document's summary of the check is rewritten to match what it does, stating coverage by location rather than by claim kind, and listing the properties rounds 8 through 10 added.

suggestion: Restate that paragraph of spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md from the script's current COVERAGE string and its current failure conditions, or cut the description and point at the script, so the boundary has a single home -- §8.1's rule applied to this release's own artifact.

finding: The new paragraph divides responsibility between two observers and, as written, neither one observes — so it reads as a disclaimer where a requirement belongs. (a) The half it credits to the tool: "`scripts/check-measured-claims.py` compares the written list against the derivation as a set … it reports `PENDING` until the list exists." The check is registered as `workflow.checks` in `spec/0.34.0.tasks.json`, and registered checks execute from exactly three call sites, all in the review phase (`review.go:532`, `review_status.go:73`, `review_regression.go:102`); no audit, close, `tp done` or quality-gate path reads `Checks`. The list is written by the first implementation task, i.e. after review converges — so the set comparison this paragraph credits is, in every automated channel this release has, never run against a written list. PENDING is not one state of the check; under the release's own wiring it is the only state the check will ever be observed in. (b) The half it assigns to the task: "The observer for that rule is the first task's own acceptance." §7.1 states no content for that acceptance, and §12's partition of the spec into outcome sections (§3, §4, §5, §8.2, §8.3, §9) and judgement sections (§6.2, §6.3, §7.2, §7.3, §8.1) does not include §7.1, so no acceptance shape is mandated for it either. Two engineers write materially different acceptances — "the file exists and is populated" versus "the entry set equals the derivation and the check exits 0 with no PENDING line" — and both satisfy the paragraph. Contrast §5, which faces the same problem and closes it in one sentence by stating what the guard must compare against what. The last sentence, "Closing that task with an empty list is therefore a decision a human makes, not one the check can prevent", then names an actor with no seat in the loop: §2 does route judgement to the operator explicitly ("it is the operator's call"), but this task closes through `tp done` run by the unit, and nothing surfaces the empty list to a human for that decision.

resolved.evidence: Section 7.1 now gives that acceptance its content: run the check to exit 0 with no PENDING line, which is reachable only after the list is written and the placeholder deleted. It also records why the task must be the observer -- registered checks run in the review phase only, while the list is written afterwards.

suggestion: Keep the honesty and add the one pin it is missing: state that the first task's acceptance must require `scripts/check-measured-claims.py` to exit 0 with no `PENDING` line emitted, run after the list is written — that is a deterministic assertion, it converts PENDING from a permanent state into a transition the task must complete, and it gives §12 the acceptance shape §7.1 currently has in neither of its two lists. If the empty-list decision is genuinely reserved to a human, say which artifact carries it (the closing evidence, per §2.1) rather than leaving "a decision a human makes" as the whole mechanism.

finding: The paragraph added to §7.1 since round 9 describes what scripts/check-measured-claims.py does, and it is already wrong about it -- in the direction that understates the guard the round-8/9 repairs built. Measured on a clone at 66ec712: 'it reports PENDING until the list exists' holds only while the 'Populated by the first task' declaration is present; with that declaration deleted and no entries written the check exits 1 ('no list entries and no ... declaration. An empty guard list is a failed derivation, never a result'), and with entries written alongside the declaration it also exits 1. The closing claim -- 'Closing that task with an empty list is therefore a decision a human makes, not one the check can prevent' -- is therefore false for exactly the arrangement the guard doc's own protocol produces ('Delete the declaration when the list is written'); the check does prevent it there, and the residual gap is only the narrower case of a list left unwritten with the declaration intact. Two structural problems compound the inaccuracy: this makes a third home for one fact (the script docstring, spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md, and now §7.1), which is the drift §8.1 exists to end and which the two homes already disagree in (see the sibling finding); and it is mechanism whose correctness can only be established against code, which §12 states belongs in task acceptance rather than in the spec -- the same reason §12's numbered test list was deleted after four rounds of the section and its restatement overturning each other.

resolved.evidence: Same repair as index 2: the paragraph states an acceptance requirement rather than describing tool behaviour, and the description of what the check does moved to the guard document.

suggestion: Keep the policy sentence -- the observer for the empty-list rule is the first task's own acceptance -- and drop the two sentences describing what the check compares and reports. If the residual gap must be named, name it as the case it actually is: a guard list left unwritten with the placeholder declaration intact passes the check, so only the task's acceptance can tell 'not yet derived' from 'derived to nothing'.
